edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 1, Paris 1844), Ad martyres, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Caetera aeque animi impedimenta usque ad limen carceris deduxerint vos, quousque et parentes vestri. Exinde segragati est is ab ipso mundo, quanto magis a saeculo, rebusque ejus? Nec hoc vos consternet, quod segregati estis a mundo. Si enim recogitemus ipsum magis mundum carcerem esse, exisse vos e carcere, quam in carcerem introisse, intelligemus. Majores tenebras habet mundus, quae hominum praecordia excaecant. Graviores catenas induit mundus, quae ipsas animas hominum constringunt. Pejores immunditias exspirat mundus, libidines hominum. Plures postremo mundus reos continet, scilicet universum hominum genus. Judicia denique non proconsulis, sed Dei sustinet. Quo vos, benedicti, de carcere in custodiarium si forte translatos existimetis. Habet tenebras, sed lumen estis ipsi: habet vincula, sed vos soluti Deo estis. Triste illic exspirat, sed vos odor estis suavitatis; Judex exspectatur, sed vos estis de judicibus ipsis judicaturi. Contristetur illic, qui fructum saeculi suspirat. Christianus etiam extra carcerem saeculo renuntiavit, in carcere autem etiam carceri. Nihil interest, ubi sitis in saeculo, qui extra saeculum estis; et si aliqua amisistis vitae gaudia, negotiatio est aliquid amittere, ut majora lucreris. Nihil adhuc dico de praemio, ad quod Deus martyres invitat. Ipsam interim conversationem saeculi et carceris comparemus, si non plus in carcere spiritus acquirit quam caro amittit, imo et quae justa sunt caro non amittit per curam Ecclesiae, agapen fratrum: et insuper quae semper utilia fidei, spiritus adipiscitur. Non vides alienos deos, non imaginibus eorum incurris, non solemnes nationum dies ipsa commixtione participas, non nidoribus spurcis verberaris, non clamoribus spectaculorum, atrocitate, vel furore, vel impudicitia celebrantium caederis: non in loca libidinum publicarum oculi tui impingunt: vacas a scandalis, a tentationibus, a recordationibus malis, jam et a persecutione. Hoc praestat carcer christiano, quod eremus prophetis. Ipse Dominus in secessu frequentius agebat, ut liberius oraret, ut saeculo cederet. Gloriam denique suam discipulis in solitudine demonstravit. Auferamus carceris nomen, secessum vocemus. Etsi corpus includitur, etsi caro detinetur, omnia spiritui patent. Vagare spiritu, spatiare spiritu, et non stadia opaca aut porticus longas praeponens tibi, sed illam viam, quae ad Deum ducit. Quotiens eam spiritu deambulaveris, totiens in carcere non eris. Nihil crus sentit in nervo cum animus in coelo est. Totum hominem animus circumfert, et quo velit transfert: Ubi autem erit cor tuum, illic erit et thesaurus tuus. Ibi ergo sit cor nostrum, ubi volumus habere thesaurum.
pass_a_gloss: Other things have led you equally as hindrances of the mind up to the threshold of prison, as far as also your parents. From that point on, he is separated from the world itself, how much more from the age and its things? And this should not disturb you, that you are separated from the world. For if we consider that the world itself is a greater prison, you have gone out of prison, rather than entered into prison, we will understand. The world has greater darknesses, which blind the hearts of men. The world wears heavier chains, which constrain the very souls of men. The world breathes out worse impurities, the lusts of men. Finally, the world contains more guilty ones, namely the whole human race. It undergoes judgments, not of the proconsul, but of God. To what extent you, blessed ones, think that you have been transferred from prison to a guardhouse, if perhaps. It has darkness, but you are the light: it has bonds, but you are freed to God. There it breathes out sadness, but you are the odor of sweetness. A judge is expected, but you are to judge among the judges themselves. He is saddened there, who sighs for the fruit of the age. A Christian has also renounced the age, even outside of prison, but in prison, he has renounced prison as well. It makes no difference where you are in the age, who are outside of the age. And if you have lost some joys of life, it is a business to lose something, so that you may gain greater things. I am not yet speaking about the reward, to which God invites martyrs. Let us compare for the time being the very conversation of the age and of prison, if the spirit does not acquire more in prison than the flesh loses, indeed even what is just the flesh does not lose through the care of the Church, the love of brothers. And furthermore, what is always useful to faith, the spirit acquires. You do not see foreign gods, you do not run into their images, you do not participate in the solemn days of nations by your very mixing, you are not beaten by filthy smells, you are not struck by the shouts of spectacles, the cruelty, or the fury, or the shamelessness of those celebrating. Your eyes do not strike against public places of lust. You are free from scandals, from temptations, from evil recollections, and now even from persecution. This is what prison provides for a Christian, what the desert provided for prophets. The Lord himself acted more frequently in solitude, so that he might pray more freely, so that he might yield to the age. Finally, he showed his glory to his disciples in solitude. Let us take away the name of prison, let us call it solitude. Even if the body is enclosed, even if the flesh is detained, all things are open to the spirit. To wander in spirit, to walk in spirit, and not preferring dark stadiums or long porticos to you, but that way, which leads to God. As often as you walk in spirit on it, so often you will not be in prison. The leg does not feel the nerve when the mind is in heaven. The mind carries the whole man around and transfers him where it wills. Where your heart will be, there your treasure will also be. Therefore, let our heart be there, where we want to have our treasure.
pass_b_english: Other hindrances of the mind have led you right up to the prison threshold, just as they led your parents. From that point on, he is cut off from the world itself — how much more from the age and all that belongs to it? And this should not shake you: you have been separated from the world. If we stop to consider that the world itself is the greater prison, we will see that you have actually left prison, not entered it. The world holds a deeper darkness, the kind that blinds men's hearts. It clamps heavier chains, the kind that bind men's very souls. It exhales fouler impurities — men's lusts. In the end, it holds more prisoners: the whole human race. And it awaits judgment not from a proconsul, but from God. So why, you blessed ones, would you think you've been transferred from prison to a mere guardhouse? The place has darkness, but you are the light; it has chains, but you have been set free for God. It breathes misery, but you are the fragrance of sweetness. A judge is expected there, but you are the ones who will sit among the judges themselves. Let the man who sighs for the world's rewards be the one who is saddened. A Christian has already renounced the world even outside prison; inside prison, he renounces the prison itself. It makes no difference where you are in the world, you who stand outside it. And if you have lost some of life's joys, think of it as a transaction: you lose something to gain far more. I am not even touching yet on the reward to which God calls martyrs. Let us simply compare, for now, the daily reality of the world against that of prison. Does the spirit not gain more in prison than the flesh loses? Indeed, the flesh does not even lose what is rightfully its own, thanks to the Church's care and the brothers' love. On top of that, the spirit acquires everything that faith finds useful. You do not see foreign gods; you do not stumble over their images; you do not take part in the nations' holy days by mere presence; you are not battered by filthy stenches; you are not struck by the roars of spectacles — their cruelty, their fury, their shamelessness. Your eyes do not fall on public brothels. You are free from scandals, from temptations, from evil memories, and now even from persecution. This is what prison gives a Christian — what the desert gave the prophets. The Lord himself withdrew into solitude more often, so he could pray more freely, so he could yield to the age. Finally, he revealed his glory to his disciples in solitude. So let us drop the name 'prison' and call it solitude. Even if the body is shut in, even if the flesh is detained, everything stands open to the spirit. Wander in the spirit, walk in the spirit — not preferring dark stadiums or long porticoes, but choosing that way which leads to God. As often as you walk it in spirit, that often you are not in prison. The leg feels no pain in the nerve when the mind is in heaven. The mind carries the whole man wherever it wishes. Where your heart is, there your treasure will be also. So let our heart be where we want our treasure to be.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text, including the distinction between the world (saeculum) and the age, the passive voice of 'segregati estis', and the theological implications of the spirit vs. flesh. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Locked Latin.
